lesson.title: Build a Better ls CLI in Rust with Clap
lesson.goal: build a command-line tool in Rust with cargo that parses arguments

goalMatch.note: This code-along builds a Rust CLI app with crates via cargo, which very likely includes argument parsing (e.g., clap), though the description doesn't confirm it explicitly.

sources.title: Build a Better ls CLI in Rust with Clap

steps.title: Create project and parse path argument
steps.instructions: Run `cargo new best_ls`, add clap with the derive feature to Cargo.toml, and define a `#[derive(Parser)]` struct with an optional `PathBuf` path parsed via `Cli::parse()` in main. Verify with `cargo run -- -h` showing the usage line and path argument.

targets.caption: Add clap with the derive feature
Cli struct with an optional PathBuf path
Auto-generated help from cargo run -- -h

explanations.topic: clap derive feature makes argument parsing easy
Deriving Parser adds the parse() method
Using -- to pass arguments through cargo run
Reading the generated usage/arguments/options help

hints: Make sure clap is in [dependencies] with features = ["derive"].
Add #[derive(Parser)] above your Cli struct and import it with use clap::Parser;.
path should be Option<PathBuf>; import std::path::PathBuf.
Run cargo run -- -h — the -- separates cargo's flags from your program's.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the derive feature on clap, so #[derive(Parser)] doesn't exist
Not importing clap::Parser, so Cli::parse() is not found
Running cargo run -h (shows cargo's help) instead of cargo run -- -h
Missing use std::path::PathBuf

steps.title: Add version, about, default path
steps.instructions: Add `#[command(version, about, long_about = ...)]` to the Cli struct, then default the path with `cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from("."))` and print `path.display()`. Check `cargo run -- --version` and `cargo run -- long_path`.

targets.caption: Add version, about and long_about
Default the path to "."
Build finishes and prints the path

explanations.topic: #[command(version)] auto-generates a --version flag
long_about text appears in the --help output
The path is an Option, so unwrap_or supplies a default
Defaulting to "." means the current directory, like ls

hints: Put the #[command(...)] attribute right under #[derive(Parser)] on your Cli struct.
Try `cargo run -- --version` and `cargo run -- --help` to see what clap generates.
cli.path is an Option<PathBuf>; use .unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")) to get a value.
PathBuf doesn't implement Display, so print it with path.display().
common_mistakes: Forgetting the `--` in `cargo run -- --version`, so cargo consumes the flag instead of your program.
Writing #[clap(...)] or #[command] above #[derive(Parser)] instead of below it.
Trying println!("{}", path) directly, which fails because PathBuf isn't Display.
Missing `use std::path::PathBuf;` so PathBuf::from doesn't compile.
Putting the default as a &str instead of PathBuf, causing a type mismatch in unwrap_or.

steps.title: Check path existence with colors
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs use `if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path)` and print "Path does not exist" in red via owo-colors `.red()`, or "Error reading directory" on Err. Run `cargo run -- nonexistent` to see the red message.

targets.caption: Check whether the path exists
Add the owo-colors crate
Red message for a missing path

explanations.topic: fs::exists tells you whether a path exists
Adding the owo-colors crate to print colored output
cargo build puts the debug binary in target/debug
fs::exists returns Err when existence can't be confirmed or denied

hints: Use `if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path)` and branch on `does_exist`.
Add `owo-colors` under [dependencies] in Cargo.toml (or run `cargo add owo-colors`).
Bring the trait into scope with `use owo_colors::OwoColorize;`, then call `"Path does not exist".red()` inside println!.
Add an `else` branch for the Err case that prints "Error reading directory", then run `cargo run -- nonexistent`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting `use owo_colors::OwoColorize;`, so `.red()` is not found.
Writing the crate name as `owo_colors` in Cargo.toml instead of `owo-colors`.
Typing `if let ok(...)` instead of `Ok`, which the presenter also stumbled on.
Running `cargo run nonexistent` without `--`, which works but is easy to confuse with cargo flags.
Not handling the Err case, so a permission error falls through silently.

steps.title: List directory file names
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs write `fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String>` that iterates `fs::read_dir(path)` and pushes each `file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())`. In main loop over `get_files(&path)`, print each name, then run `cargo run`.

targets.caption: New helper that returns the file names in a directory
Convert the OsString name with a fallback
File names from the directory are printed

explanations.topic: Designing get_files to return Vec<String> first and expand it later
if let Ok on fs::read_dir and iterating entries
file_name().into_string() and fallback with unwrap_or
cargo run with no argument defaults to current directory

hints: Write a separate function that takes a &Path and returns Vec<String>. Call it from main only when the path exists.
Use `if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path)`, then loop with `for entry in read_dir`. Each entry is a Result, so unwrap it with `if let Ok(file) = entry`.
`file.file_name()` returns an OsString. Call `.into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())` to get a String.
In main, write `for file in get_files(&path) { println!("{}", file); }`. Then run `cargo run` with no arguments.
common_mistakes: Forgetting `use std::fs;` or `use std::path::Path;`, which gives an unresolved name error.
Passing `path` (a PathBuf) instead of `&path` to get_files, which gives a mismatched types error.
Not declaring the vector with `let mut`, so `push` fails to compile.
Calling `.to_string()` on the OsString, which doesn't exist, instead of `.into_string()`.
Ending the function with `return data;` inside the if block only, so nothing is returned when read_dir fails.

steps.title: Collect metadata into FileEntry structs
steps.instructions: Define `struct FileEntry` and `enum EntryType { File, Dir }` deriving strum's Display, filled in a `map_data` function via `fs::metadata(&file.path())`. Pretty-print the Vec with `{:#?}` and run `cargo run`.

targets.caption: Struct holding each file's metadata
File/Dir enum deriving strum Display
Extracted mapping function
Pretty-printed metadata output

explanations.topic: Designing a struct to hold file metadata
Using an enum for entry type and strum's Display derive
fs::metadata returns a Result, so match Ok with if let
Bug: passing the directory path instead of file.path()
Extracting the mapping into map_data

hints: Add a struct with name, e_type, len_bytes (u64) and modified (String) fields, and an enum with File and Dir variants.
Add strum (with the derive feature) to Cargo.toml, derive Display on the enum, and derive Debug on both types so {:#?} works.
Inside the loop, use `if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(&file.path())`, then set e_type with `if meta.is_dir() { EntryType::Dir } else { EntryType::File }` and len_bytes with `meta.len()`.
Move the push logic into `fn map_data(file: fs::DirEntry, data: &mut Vec<FileEntry>)` and print the vector with `println!("{:#?}", ...)`.
common_mistakes: Passing the directory `path` to fs::metadata instead of `file.path()`, so every entry shows the same metadata.
Matching `Some(meta)` instead of `Ok(meta)`: fs::metadata returns a Result, not an Option.
Naming a field `type`. It is a reserved keyword, so use something like e_type.
Forgetting #[derive(Debug)] on FileEntry or EntryType, which makes {:#?} fail to compile.
Adding strum without the `derive` feature (or without strum_macros), so `use strum::Display` doesn't resolve.
Changing the function's return type to Vec<FileEntry> without also changing the vector it builds.

steps.title: Print a styled colored table
steps.instructions: Add the tabled crate, derive `Tabled` on FileEntry, build `Table::new(...)` with `Style::rounded()` and column/row colors, and rename headers with `#[tabled(rename = ...)]`. Run `cargo run` to see the colored table.

targets.caption: Build the table from get_files
Color columns and header row
Rename table headers
Renamed header in output

explanations.topic: What the tabled crate does: pretty ASCII tables from structs
Table::new replaces the manual print loop
Applying a table Style (rounded)
modify() with Columns/Rows targets and Color foregrounds
Renaming headers with #[tabled(rename)]

hints: Add tabled to Cargo.toml (cargo add tabled) and derive Tabled on FileEntry alongside Debug.
Replace the for-loop with let mut table = Table::new(get_files(&path)); then println!("{}", table).
Use table.with(Style::rounded()) and table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN); Rows::first() targets the header row.
Every field type in a Tabled struct must implement Display — implement Display for your EntryType enum if the compiler complains.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to derive Tabled on FileEntry, so Table::new won't compile.
EntryType enum not implementing Display, causing a trait-bound error.
Declaring table without mut, so with()/modify() fail.
Importing Style/Color/Columns/Rows from the wrong module path (they live under tabled::settings).
Writing #[tabled(rename = ...)] above the struct instead of above the field.

steps.title: Format modified dates with chrono
steps.instructions: Add chrono to Cargo.toml and in map_data use `if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified()` converting to `DateTime<Utc>` and formatting with `date.format("%a %b %e %Y")`, else an empty string. Run `cargo run -- src` to see the dates.

targets.caption: Convert the SystemTime from metadata into a formatted date
Add the chrono crate as a dependency

explanations.topic: Why chrono: std lacks date/time formatting
Fallback to empty string when modified time unavailable
meta.modified() returns Result<SystemTime>
Converting SystemTime into DateTime<Utc> with .into()
strftime-style format specifiers

hints: Add chrono to [dependencies] in Cargo.toml (e.g. `cargo add chrono`).
meta.modified() returns a Result, so use `if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() { ... } else { String::default() }`.
Annotate the conversion: `let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into();` and import with `use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};`.
Return `date.format("%a %b %e %Y").to_string()` and run `cargo run -- src`.
common_mistakes: Naming the binding `mod`, which is a reserved Rust keyword (the presenter switches to `modi`).
Calling `.into()` without a type annotation, so the compiler can't infer DateTime<Utc>.
Forgetting `use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};` and getting unresolved type errors.
Not adding chrono to Cargo.toml, causing 'unresolved import chrono'.
Making the if branch and else branch return different types (e.g. &str vs String).

steps.title: Add --json flag with serde
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs add `#[arg(short, long)] json: bool` to Cli, move table printing into `print_table`, derive `Serialize` on FileEntry and EntryType, and when `cli.json` print `serde_json::to_string(&get_files(&path))`. Verify with `cargo run -- -j` and `cargo run -- --json`.

targets.caption: New --json / -j flag on the Cli struct
Table printing extracted into its own function
Serialize the file entries to JSON
JSON output of the file entries

explanations.topic: short/long clap args give both -j and --json flags
serde with derive plus serde_json to serialize data to JSON
Serialize must be derived on the enum too, not just the struct
unwrap_or supplies a fallback string if serialization fails

hints: Add a `json: bool` field to your Cli struct and annotate it with `#[arg(short, long)]` so clap generates -j and --json.
Move your table-printing code into a `print_table` function, then branch on `if cli.json { ... } else { print_table(...) }`.
Run `cargo add serde --features derive` and `cargo add serde_json`, then add `Serialize` to the derive list on both FileEntry and EntryType (import `serde::Serialize`).
Print with `println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files(&path)).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string()));` and test with `cargo run -- -j`.
common_mistakes: Adding `json: bool` without `#[arg(short, long)]`, so clap treats it as a positional arg and no -j/--json flag appears.
Deriving Serialize on FileEntry but not on EntryType, which causes a 'trait bound Serialize is not satisfied' compile error.
Adding serde without the `derive` feature, so `#[derive(Serialize)]` cannot be found.
Forgetting the `--` in `cargo run -- -j`, so cargo tries to interpret -j itself.
Serializing a value that was already moved into print_table instead of calling get_files again (or borrowing).
